cross_component_finding: This is the one page in the batch where guide-level content most directly overlaps a reference page's own explanatory text: the 'Setting the Query Context' section here restates, in slightly different words and with added UI-tab instructions (Query Tab vs CBQ Shell), the same query-context mechanism documented in cloud/n1ql/n1ql-intro/queriesandresults.md (linked explicitly at the end: 'For more information and examples, see Query Context'). The core factual content (query context resolves partial keyspace references; \SET/\UNSET with query_context) is consistent between the two pages - no contradictory wording found - but this is the clearest candidate in the batch for the round's watched-for content-duplication risk: a guide page giving its own worked explanation of a concept that a reference page also fully explains, rather than only linking to it. Every other guide page in this batch (insert/delete/update/reading/creating/etc.) links to this same #query-context anchor rather than re-explaining it, so the duplication is contained to this one origin point.
